200.body: Polish president backs down and approves government’s windfall tax on fuel companies Oct 2, 2026 | Business , Law , Politics Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! The government had been pushing the president to approve the measures amid soaring fuel prices. Since then, he and the government have been locked in a dispute over the issue, with Prime Minister Donald Tusk arguing that measures to reduce fuel prices, which were briefly reintroduced in the last two weeks of August , can only be restored if Nawrocki signs the windfall tax. President @NawrockiKn has obstructed a planned windfall tax on fuel companies by sending it to the constitutional court, where it could stay for years The tax aimed to offset fuel price protection costs after the Iran war surge https://t.co/UojVuYhvdV — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 27, 2026 In September, the government’s majority in parliament passed the windfall tax bill a second time.

300.summary: Business European News Europe’s Big Four All Beat Inflation Forecasts, and Stock Markets Are Paying the Price By EBM Newsdesk - October 2, 2026 0 21 Facebook Twitter Pinterest WhatsApp London, 2 October 2026 — EBM Newsdesk Analysis — By Anthony Gill On Friday, 2nd October, European equities traded lower, with losses spread across most sectors.
300.body: Business European News Europe’s Big Four All Beat Inflation Forecasts, and Stock Markets Are Paying the Price By EBM Newsdesk - October 2, 2026 0 21 Facebook Twitter Pinterest WhatsApp London, 2 October 2026 — EBM Newsdesk Analysis — By Anthony Gill On Friday, 2nd October, European equities traded lower, with losses spread across most sectors. September inflation in Germany, France, Italy and Spain all came in above forecasts, keeping pressure on the European Central Bank to raise rates again. Traders continue to price in another rate rise before the end of the year, as the ECB’s long fight against eurozone inflation drags on. European markets can absorb one bad inflation print, but not a run of them alongside rising bond yields and a fragile France.

300.title: Polish students face a changing job market amid AI boom
300.summary: Polish students began a new academic year on Thursday with artificial intelligence increasingly shaping how they think about their studies and future careers. First-year students at Warsaw University of Technology told TVP World they were entering university hoping to gain practical experience and professional contacts, but some also voiced concerns about how automation could affect their job prospects.
300.body: Polish students began a new academic year on Thursday with artificial intelligence increasingly shaping how they think about their studies and future careers. First-year students at Warsaw University of Technology told TVP World they were entering university hoping to gain practical experience and professional contacts, but some also voiced concerns about how automation could affect their job prospects. Izabela Grabowska, a professor at Kozminski University, said students should focus on lifelong learning and learn to work alongside AI rather than compete with it. “For students who are starting today, the most important advice is not to compete with AI but to work with AI,” Grabowska said.

Which brings us back to July. .contents]:contents flex items-center" data-empty-mobile="true"> OpenAI dropped thousands of agents into isolated sandboxes to run capture-the-flag challenges.
500.body: The “swarm” of OpenAI agents that went rogue in July has reignited an existential debate about artificial intelligence and its potential to one day overtake, or even destroy, humanity . Multi-agent systems (from Microsoft’s AutoGen to Claude Research’s subagents) have achieved limited coordination in this way over the past few years. .contents]:contents flex items-center" data-empty-desktop="true"> We humans swarm when a street mob riots or when holiday shoppers stampede. Which brings us back to July. .contents]:contents flex items-center" data-empty-mobile="true"> OpenAI dropped thousands of agents into isolated sandboxes to run capture-the-flag challenges. It will arrive when the agents cease working alone and strive for the collective intelligence that humans enjoy. .contents]:contents flex items-center" data-empty-mobile="true"> The question isn’t whether they’ll become human.
